declared_proposition: Let a_k=C(17,k)2^floor(k/2) and B_1(u,v)=sum_(k=0)^17 a_k u^(17-k)v^k. Put A=sum a_k=2744210 and V_0=(A+1)16^9=188580743973175296. For coprime nonzero integers u,v with v>V_0 and 1/16<=|u|/v<=1, and epsilon in {-1,1}, B_1(u,v)=epsilon if and only if the first nine terms are epsilon modulo v^9 and the last nine terms are epsilon modulo u^9.
mathematical_argument: Necessity follows by deleting terms divisible by v^9 or u^9. Conversely the joint congruences and gcd(u,v)=1 imply (|uv|)^9 divides B_1(u,v)-epsilon. Since |u|<=v, positivity of the coefficients gives |B_1-epsilon|<=(A+1)v^17. The cone gives (|uv|)^9>=v^18/16^9, which is strictly larger when v>V_0. A nonzero divisible integer cannot have smaller absolute value than its divisor, so B_1-epsilon=0. Thus order nine is an exact tail criterion on this cone, not merely another necessary jet. The finite continued-fraction replay checks both signs and orders one through nine on 1024 convergents; it does not prove that every later convergent fails the ninth-order pair.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: certified rational continued fractions, exact degree-17 evaluation, and bidirectional modular truncation for orders one through nine
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(K*R*17) exact big-integer terms with moduli u^r and v^r, R=9

finite_computation_boundary: Both signs and orders one through nine are tested on 1024 certified convergents; this is finite despite reaching a 519-digit denominator.
logical_limit: The tail congruence criterion is exact on the cone, but infinitely many later convergents and the finite denominators below the explicit threshold are not globally excluded.

route_decision.discard: treating successively higher finite binomial jets as an endless source of independent necessary conditions beyond the degree-seventeen form
parked: global exclusion of the joint ninth-order congruences on every unique-root continued-fraction convergent
route_decision.retain: the explicit root-cone size threshold where the bidirectional ninth-order congruence pair is equivalent to the original unit equation

claim_boundary: No twin-prime proof or counterexample; one exponent-17 Thue branch is reduced to an exact ninth-order tail congruence test.
